justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: Video Media Server handles video consultations (R-01), Integration Service Container dispatches e-prescriptions (R-02), AI Symptom Checker Container provides triage recommendations (R-03), and Consent Policy Evaluator enforces purpose-based consent management (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance is addressed via Model Cache / Warm Loader, PyTorch/ONNX inference, Memorystore for Redis caching in Consent Policy Evaluator, Connection Pooling Component, and asynchronous event distribution via Cloud Pub/Sub and Outbox Event Processor.
justifications.compatibility: External interoperability requirements are met: EU/US E-Prescription Adapters connect to US Pharmacy Networks and EU National E-Prescription Gateways using HL7 FHIR and REST, while Regional Identity Providers integrate via standard OIDC/OAuth2.
justifications.usability: The Web & Mobile App container provides tailored UI Layer components for Patients, Clinicians, and Regional Pharmacists, backed by State & Offline Manager to handle intermittent connectivity gracefully for rural end users.
justifications.reliability: Reliability under poor network conditions is ensured by Adaptive Bitrate Controller (audio-only fallback) and State & Offline Manager. Fault tolerance is reinforced by DLQ Manager and Outbox Event Processor for message delivery.
justifications.security: Rigorous security includes mTLS between internal containers, Policy Enforcement Proxy, Encryption Service using Cloud KMS, pgaudit in Database Instance Component, and strict regional isolation enforced by Data Residency Guard and Consent & Policy Interceptor.
justifications.maintainability: High maintainability is achieved through decoupled containers with distinct responsibilities (Core Services, AI Symptom Checker, Integration Service) and modular design using Prescription Router and EU/US E-Prescription Adapters.
justifications.portability: The design targets GCP regions europe-west3 and us-central1 directly using Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage Buckets, paired with portable containerized stacks (Spring Boot, Node.js, FastAPI, Go) and cross-platform Flutter UI Layer.

PERF-01.justification: LiveKit SFU with in-memory token verification and NGINX signaling provides fast session establishment. However, specific SFU clustering and autoscaling mechanisms under 5,000 concurrent sessions are not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: Local token verification latency on connection setup
SFU connection handling and concurrent stream limits
tradeoffs: In-memory local token validation improves joining speed over centralized auth checks

PERF-02.justification: Peak load of 50,000 requests/hour (~14 req/s) is modest. The FastAPI router, ONNX runtime, in-memory warm model cache, and asynchronous audit logging easily satisfy the 3-second latency target.
sensitivity_points: Model execution latency in ONNX runtime
Asynchronous buffer throughput for audit logs
tradeoffs: In-memory model caching consumes memory to reduce cold-start inference latency

AVAIL-01.justification: The Adaptive Bitrate Controller dynamically degrades video to audio-only on 200 kbit/s links, and the client-side State & Offline Manager uses SQLCipher/IndexedDB to prevent any loss of clinical notes.
sensitivity_points: Client-side offline storage consistency and synchronization
tradeoffs: Sacrificing video feeds preserves continuous audio communication under severe bandwidth constraints

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture defines only a single US region (us-central1). Because data residency strictly forbids failing over US data to the EU, an outage of us-central1 cannot be restored within 1 hour without a secondary US region.
sensitivity_points: Single US region deployment lack of intra-national redundancy
Strict data residency rules preventing cross-region failover
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents compliance violations but impairs disaster recovery without multi-region pairing

MOD-01.justification: The Integration Service Container isolates external integrations through a dedicated Prescription Router and pluggable EU/US E-Prescription Adapters, ensuring new national EU standards require changes only to a single adapter component.
sensitivity_points: Standardization of internal canonical e-prescription data formats across adapters
tradeoffs: Adapter encapsulation increases layer hops but isolates national external API changes

MOD-02.justification: The Model Cache / Warm Loader facilitates model updates, while the Audit & Traceability Logger persists inputs, outputs, and model versions to Cloud Storage for MDR compliance. Automated runtime rollback orchestration is not fully detailed.
sensitivity_points: Atomic model version tagging across inference runs and audit trails
tradeoffs: Persisting complete inference inputs and model metadata increases logging volume for compliance

SEC-01.justification: Multi-tier mechanisms enforce this: the Policy Enforcement Proxy intercepts cross-region requests, the Consent Policy Evaluator checks permissions, the Data Residency Auditor enforces boundaries, and all attempts are recorded via the Audit Logger.
sensitivity_points: Freshness and cache invalidation latency of consent policies in Redis
tradeoffs: Multi-layer consent and residency checks increase request latency to guarantee compliance

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are processed by the Consent Policy Evaluator and logged by the Audit Logger. However, the architecture lacks background mechanisms or pipelines to invalidate or purge previously shared data from downstream research stores.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of revoked consent across cached layers and batch pipelines
tradeoffs: Immediate distributed cache invalidation ensures timely compliance but increases load on primary databases
